sentences.text: Zhuchengtyrannus was a large carnivorous theropod estimated to be about 10 meters in body length and 5 metric tons in body mass.
David W. E. Hone and colleagues first described and named this animal in 2011.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was collected from the Zangjiazhuang quarry in Zhucheng City, dating to at least 73.5 million years ago.
Zhuchengtyrannus belongs to the parent group Tyrannosaurini.
It is classified in the family Tyrannosauridae.
A 2013 phylogenetic analysis recovered Zhuchengtyrannus as the sister taxon of Tarbosaurus.
Research suggests Zhuchengtyrannus and other Asian tyrannosaurids descended from a North American stem lineage that later gave rise to Tyrannosaurus rex.
A 2024 study found Zhuchengtyrannus to be the closest relative of Tarbosaurus.
Zhuchengtyrannus lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in Shandong Province, China.
This animal lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
It is debated whether isolated teeth from the 1970s named Tyrannosaurus zhuchengensis belong to Zhuchengtyrannus or a related species.
